note: Namibia: holders of the ordinary passports listed enter without a visa for 3 months a calendar year; nationals of the EU, the US, the UK and the many others listed get a 90-day visa on arrival (N$1,600, N$1,200 for Africans; since 1 April 2025 for the Western countries whose exemption ended); everyone else applies for an e-Visa. Read from Wikipedia's copy. Checked on 2026-11-03 against the Ministry of Home Affairs' fact sheet (version 4, dated 28 May 2025, read as page images) and the High Commission in London: they confirmed the 22 exempt (3 months a calendar year) and 88 of the visa-on-arrival list, and add Ghana, which was added; the 29 others Wikipedia's copy listed (among them Cyprus, Malta and Slovenia) aren't on the fact sheet, whose note sends them to the e-Visa, and Wikipedia's sources for them are older than it, so they were moved to the e-Visa.

sources.title: Wikipedia, Visa policy of Namibia
sources.said: Holders of ordinary passports issued by the following jurisdictions can enter Namibia without a visa for a maximum stay of 3 months within any 1 calendar year: Angola Botswana Brazil Cuba Eswatini Hong Kong Indonesia Jamaica Kenya Lesotho Macao Malawi Malaysia Mauritius Mozambique Russia Seychelles Singapore South Africa Tanzania Zambia Zimbabwe ... Cancelled 1 April 2025: Armenia, Australia, Austria, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Belgium, Canada, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Iceland, Ireland, Italy, Japan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Moldova, Netherlands, New Zealand, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uzbekistan, United Kingdom, United States ... Citizens of the following countries and territories can obtain a visa on arrival for a maximum stay of 90 days. The cost of the visa on arrival is N$ 1,600 (approximately € 82 / US$ 88) for citizens of non-African countries and N$1,200 (approximately €62 / US$66) for nationals of African countries. sources.title: High Commission of the Republic of Namibia, London: Visa Fees and Exemptions
sources.said: As of the 1 August 2016, all citizens of countries with which Namibia has VISA Exemption Agreements will be allowed to enter into Namibia for no longer than three (3) months per calendar year and will get Visitor's Entry Permit (VEP) endorsement stamps at the Port of entry
